mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing state is not party to the Apostille Convention, consular legalization through the Swiss Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official registry or authorized corporate agent in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; alternatively consular legalization for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the foreign parent/shareholder authorizing Swiss incorporation and appointment of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or shareholders' meeting of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in country of origin, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national identity copies of founders, shareholders, directors and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent state authority in the individual's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in country of origin; Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required by the Swiss notary or AML file

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Swiss certified translation of all non-German corporate documents into German
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified Swiss translator or court-sworn translation service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's certificate and notarization of the translator's signature; apostille only if required by the destination register office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP, OFAC, UN Security Council, Swiss SECO, and domestic regulatory enforcement list screening of all founders, shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs. Screening must be performed at intake and refreshed upon any material change or adverse media trigger. For the target low-risk ISIC 5210 fulfilment model, simplified due diligence may apply under AMLO, but UBO identification, legalization, and sanctions screening cannot be waived.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (zefix.ch) and the Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must comply with Swiss Code of Obligations principles of truthfulness and non-misleading form. The Canton of Zug registers in German; therefore the primary commercial name must be in Latin script, normally in German, French, Italian, or an accepted internationally comprehensible form. Non-Latin script names, e.g., simplified Chinese, must be transliterated into Latin characters for the registered firm name; the transliterated name must be pronounceable and distinguishable from existing registered names. The legal form suffix 'AG' or the French/Italian equivalent 'SA'/'SpA' is mandatory for an Aktiengesellschaft.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Bankier, Sparkasse - prohibited without FINMA banking license
Versicherung, Assurance, Insurance, Reinsurance, Rückversicherung - prohibited without FINMA insurance supervision
Fondsleitung, Anlagestiftung, kollektive Kapitalanlage - prohibited without corresponding financial market authorisation
Trust, Trustee, Fiduciary, Treuhand - restricted; may misleadingly imply financial intermediary licensing or require registration under FinIA
Rechtsanwalt, Attorney at Law, Notar, Patentanwalt, Wirtschaftsprüfer, Audit - reserved to licensed professionals
Swiss, Schweizer, Suisse, Svizzero, Helvetia, Eidgenossenschaft, Confédération, Federal - restricted by Swissness rules and public-authority non-confusion rules
Kanton Zug, Gemeinde Zug, official coats of arms or authority marks - prohibited or require cantonal consent
International organization names and emblems, including United Nations, WTO, WHO, ICRC, and Red Cross - prohibited or require prior consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name may be reserved for 180 days and, on justified request, extended for one further 180-day period by the responsible cantonal Commercial Register Office. If the name application is rejected, the applicant may first submit a written objection or amended name proposal to the Handelsregisteramt Zug. A final negative ruling may be appealed within 30 days to the cantonal supervisory authority (Directorate of Economic Affairs of Canton Zug), then to the Federal Administrative Court, and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court. In parallel, private name disputes may be pursued before the ordinary civil courts under Swiss trademark and unfair competition law.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 5210 cross-dock overseas warehouse and 3PL fulfilment company, a pure virtual office or letterbox address is not sufficient commercial substance. A managed office or licensed domiciliation provider may satisfy registered-office formalities if the company has a demonstrable Swiss administrative seat, decision-making presence, lease evidence, payroll, and operational substance. The physical fulfilment warehouse and 3PL operation must have a real Swiss or regional operational presence; virtual office arrangements can only support administration and cannot replace the substantive cross-dock logistics function from a commercial register, tax, and anti-base-erosion perspective.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but not negligible: estimated under 10% probability of unannounced on-site inspection during the first three years for a standard low-risk, non-financial 3PL entity. The probability may increase to 15-30% if the company relies solely on a domiciliation address, applies for tax incentives, holds customs bonds or licensed customs warehousing, or triggers AML/CFT and sanctions screening flags. Inspection would focus on actual administration, lease, payroll, UBO records, and operational substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Arts. 620–763 (stock corporation); specifically Art. 626 (articles of association), Art. 629 (capital requirements), Art. 635 (incorporation report), Art. 640 (registration declaration); Art. 643 (public registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) under the supervision of the Federal Commercial Register Authority (FOCER)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized declaration of incorporation (Gründungserklärung / Déclaration de fondation) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts) filed for registration in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% (CHF 20,000) must be effectively paid in cash or in kind before registration; if a one-person AG, the full capital must be covered at registration. Cash contributions must be held in a blocked escrow account at a Swiss bank or post office until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital of CHF 100,000 is deemed subscribed in full and that the board shall verify the lawful coverage of consideration under Article 632 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office shall be at [address], Switzerland, and the board is authorized to submit the declaration of incorporation to the Commercial Register; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chair of the Board, [Name] Chief Executive Officer, and [Name] Treasurer, each with individual or joint signatory rights as defined; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the board shall open a corporate bank account with [Bank] for the escrowed capital deposit and effect all statutory insurance registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association and the incorporation minutes (Gründungsprotokoll) in German, French, or Italian according to the chosen cantonal language. Have the public deed and founding declarations signed by all incorporators and notarized. Verify that the capital has been deposited in a blocked escrow account and obtain the bank's confirmation of capital coverage.
required_dossiers: Public deed of incorporation (notarized)
Articles of Association (Statuten)
List of founders with full identity details
Bank certificate confirming block and coverage of paid-up capital
Passport or identity card copies of all incorporators
Proof of registered office address (lease contract or landlord's consent)
Declaration of capital coverage signed by the board
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary will assist in correcting formal deficiencies or re-executing documents. If civil validity issues arise, amend the Articles of Association or apply to the competent cantonal court for approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with Commercial Register and Publications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized public deed, Articles of Association, board and officer details, and signed application forms to the Commercial Register electronically or by post. The registration authority verifies the completeness of the application and the compliance of the Articles of Association with the Swiss Code of Obligations. Upon acceptance, the company is registered and published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC).
required_dossiers: Notarized public deed of incorporation
Articles of Association (two copies)
Commercial Register application form signed by all board members
Declaration of authenticity of board member signatures
Confirmation of capital coverage from the bank or licensed legal entity
Consent to resign in advance from any reserve board member (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the deficiency letter (Mängelbehebung) within 10 working days by submitting the requested corrections or additional documentation. A rejection may be appealed to the cantonal court and subsequently to the Federal Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Bank and (if required) Mandatory Auditor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Register approval, instruct the bank to release the escrowed share capital into the company's free operating account. Obtain the certificate of registration (Handelsregisterauszug) to prove legal existence. If the company is subject to ordinary audit under Art. 727 CO, request the auditing firm to issue the confirmation of capital contribution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (Handelsregisterauszug)
Bank release instruction signed by the board
Board resolution specifying account controls and signing authorities
Auditor's confirmation of consideration if mandatory audit applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation or a new beneficial ownership declaration, provide the updated forms within the bank's requested timeline. In the case of a capital deficiency, the board must restore coverage by additional payments or a formal capital decrease procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Social Insurance and VAT Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Social Insurance Office (AHV/IV) and Federal Tax Administration (FTA) – VAT Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Swiss Compensation Office (AHV) for social insurance, and with SUVA for mandatory accident insurance. Apply for a VAT number and a Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) through the FTA online portal if the company's worldwide annual turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. Submit the company's registered address and corporate officer details.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
Board resolution appointing responsible officers for insurance matters
Company seal (if any)
Shareholder nationality declaration for the company register
Confirmation of workplace address for SUVA (accident insurance) tariff assignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, contact the competent compensation office or FTA to correct the application. Missing documents can be submitted by e-mail or through the online platform. Late registration fees may be waived if the company proves a justifiable deferral.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Operational Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-regulated Swiss Bank or Licensed Financial Institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the bank's KYC/AML due diligence, present the company's formation documents, and identify all beneficial owners and authorized signatories. Open the main operational account and the payroll account. Execute necessary insurances, including commercial property and liability coverage for the cross-docking facility, before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) not older than 3 months
Articles of Association
Board resolution naming bank account signatories and the company's bank relationship
Passport copies of all directors and beneficial owners
Business plan or activity description explaining the cross-dock / 3PL operating model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The bank may request additional explanations on the business model, source of funds, or beneficial ownership structure. Provide the requested information through the relationship manager. If the bank refuses the account, submit an alternative application to another licensed financial institution; no government approval is required for opening a corporate bank account.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Commerce Office (Wirtschaftsamt / Office de l'économie) with coordination by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) for occupational safety and labour law
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Warehouse Operating Permit (Betriebsbewilligung) under cantonal trade law and fire safety regulations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) with delegated enforcement to the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Amt für Umwelt)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Cross-docking and 3PL warehousing is a low-impact activity; ordinarily exempt from a full EIA and subject only to a prior environmental notification (Einfache Anzeige) unless located in a sensitive zone or exceeding 5,000 m2 of logistics floor area, in which case a simple screening (Voruntersuchung) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Swiss Waters Protection Act (GSchG), with limits for BOD5 not exceeding 5 mg/L and COD not exceeding 20 mg/L if discharged to surface waters; VOC emissions must not exceed the thresholds of the Swiss Clean Air Regulation (LRV); waste management must follow the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA); cooling installations must be free of HCFCs and other ozone-depleting substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the cantonal fire inspection authority (VKF) confirming compliance with building fire protection standards; structural load verification for storage racks and mezzanine platforms according to SIA standards; occupational health and safety inspection by the cantonal labor inspectorate or SUVA, including certification of material-handling equipment and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions – AFC). Official portal/portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; electronic filing through

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank, Banque Nationale Suisse, Banca Nazionale Svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully convertible market economy for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no surrender or conversion mandates, no central-bank authorisation for profit remittance, and no domestic FX licensing requirement for corporate treasury activities. The CHF is freely traded onshore and offshore via SWIFT, SIC/euroSIC, the Continuous Linked Settlement (CLS) system, and currency brokers. The practical hurdles for a Swiss AG in a cross-border 3PL/overseas-warehouse business are not FX-quantitative controls but (a) Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act documentation standards on account opening, (b) the 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends and participating debentures when cash is extracted, where treaty relief may reduce this rate, and (c) the obligation of the Swiss AG to be able to prove source of funds and economic substance for its inbound capital and outbound trade payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no Swiss statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory timeline for repatriation, no minimum conversion ratio into CHF, and no central-bank approval for holding export receivables offshore. Export receipts may be credited to any bank account in any currency. Only statutory reporting duties through banks for balance-of-payments statistics duties remain, but do not require currency conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (multi-currency CHF/EUR/USD)
Operational Account with dedicated e-commerce clearing and corporate e-banking
Operational Account for legacy contractural treasury services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for treasury-operations transactional use and Low for holding the Swiss AGs primary capital or reserve funds. Legal constraints: Swiss Banking Act Article 1 and Article 1b require a banking license or FINMA fintech license to commercially accept or hold public deposits in Switzerland; an EEA EMI license does not passport into Switzerland. Therefore Airwallex, Wise, Revolut Business and similar digital treasuries may be used as technical payment rails for low-value disbursements, receivables collection and conversion, but they cannot be the sole liquidity settlement venue. The key dealer/relationship bank must remain FINMA-supervised and hold the bulk liquidity in SIC-participating accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss law (AMLA Art. 3 and FINMA Circular 2016/07) requires the bank to identify the legal entity, the natural persons holding control, and any persons authorized to give payment orders. A physical sight visit by a bank relationship manager or a qualified remote identity assurance process is mandatory; directors who are non-resident are normally expected to show passport, proof of address, commercial register extract and beneficial ownership declaration, with apostilled copies where applicable. The interview can in many cases be held by video, but the bank retains discretion to require a physical meeting at a Swiss branch for high-value / capital-escrow accounts. For an operating 3PL company, remote opening with a low-KYC profile is possible only after the bank has confirmed the entity is not PEP, is not in a high-risk sector, and has the required Swiss economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is an offshore entity without audited financials, opaque ownership, or a non-resident director who cannot demonstrate source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified commercial register extract, full group-organisation chart showing natural-person controllers, current passport / residence permit, proof of address, UBO declaration under AMLA Article 4, latest audited financial statements of the direct shareholder, source-of-funds letter, bank references from the remitting institution, and where any funds derive from cryptocurrency, a FINMA-compliant exchange sequence plus chain-of-custody evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-dock / overseas 3PL model receives many small inbound e-commerce transfers from fragmented third-party marketplaces, which can trigger ambiguity regarding beneficial owners of the flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer onboarding and merchant verification policy, signed standard fulfilment services agreements, sample invoices, inventory and warehouse lease documents, intercompany service descriptions, vendor and sub-3PL licences, customs records (Swiss IMP/EXP declarations or EU ICS), an independent AML risk classification of Low_Risk_Standard, and a floor plan of the IT order-management system showing payment flows are invoiced to the Swiss AG rather than to offshore nominee accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from jurisdictions on FATF / EU / SECO sanction lists, or to foreign-exchange restricted countries, in the absence of a solid commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening logs and watchlist hits retained by the bank and treasury provider, end-user statements, export and re-export classification under the Swiss Federal Act on Exports (ECA), customs bills of lading, supplier and platform contracts, commercial LC and MT103 records, plus a written trade-compliance policy that maps SECO, SFMIA/AMLA, and OFAC re-export standards.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound capital by SWIFT MT103 or MT202COV to a SIC-participating Swiss bank account held by the Swiss AG. The beneficiary account number should be in IBAN CH format. In the payment message, include structured purpose code CAPT (capital transfer) or free text such as GELEISTETE_EINLAGE_KAPITAL_RESERVEN with a reference to the board capitalisation resolution. The receiving bank will conduct a source-of-funds and sanctions screening, and may request the underlying board minutes, contribution agreement, and evidence of the remitting bank with a valid banking licence. Because Switzerland does not levy FX controls, the capital may be contributed in CHF, EUR or USD; if the AG issues new shares, the commercial register filing will be required and capital formation proved. No SNB foreign-exchange approval is required. For amounts exceeding CHF 10,000, FINMA-compliant identification of the remitting beneficial owner is mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system for same-day CHF domestic disbursements to warehouses and staff; use euroSIC for EUR-denominated eurozone payments, and SWIFT MT103 for all non-EEA/USD trade settlements. For documentary trade, issue an irrevocable commercial letter of credit via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600, payable at sight or by deferred payment at the bank's discount; payment instructions use the 59 field for the overseas supplier and 72 field for necessary MT103 delivery. The AG may also use an EMI such as Airwallex to stream low-value cross-dock payouts to Chinese or UK merchant warehouses, but the underlying treasury must convert currency only through licensed FX counterparties and settle residual balances via bank wire. Incoterms 2020 such as DAP or FCA should be embedded in the invoices and LC documents to prevent customs interruption.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (CHF, EUR, USD, GBP) for a maximum horizon of 24 months on committed inventory purchases
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on restricted/offshore currencies (e.g. CNY, KRW, THB, IDR) where the settlement currency is USD or CHF, provided the underlying trade invoices match those currencies
FX swap / swap-forward structures to re-align cashflow legs between the warehouse operating currency and the AGs functional currency
Vanilla FX options (call or put) with zero-cost collar or standalone option premiums, reserved for approved treasury policy risks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) only where the AG has a term loan in the operating entity currency and all documentation under ISDA Master Agreement plus Credit Support Annex is in place

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) prepared, audited if applicable, and approved by the Board; presented to the Annual General Meeting for approval and discharge of the Board
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors and Annual General Meeting (internal corporate governance); no Commercial Register filing required for non-listed AG; annual accounts attached to the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM for companies with full audit: within 6 months of fiscal year-end (calendar-year company: by 30 June following year); companies with limited audit or audit opt-out: within 12 months (by 31 December); fiscal year may be a 12-month period other than the calendar year if so defined in the Articles of Association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of directors; coercive penalty up to CHF 1,000 under Art. 343 CPC; persistent absence of functioning corporate organs enables court-ordered deregistration under Art. 731b CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (Generalversammlung) resolution package: approval of accounts, elective renewal of Board, discharge of directors, re-appointment or waiver of auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate body; recorded in the corporate minute book; Commercial Register notifications follow only for changes to directors, capital, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end for full-audit companies; within 12 months for limited-audit/opt-out companies; one meeting per year is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability for damages; judicial enforcement order with penalty under Art. 343 CPC; Art. 731b CO escalation if the company becomes institutionally incapable of acting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT return (MWST/LA TVA); quarterly scheme for a standard 3PL operator; semi-annual scheme available when annual taxable turnover does not exceed CHF 5,005,000 excluding VAT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT Division, Bern
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each reporting period; calendar-year quarterly filer: Q1 by 30 May, Q2 by 30 August, Q3 by 30 November, Q4 by 28/29 February of following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge up to CHF 8,000 plus default interest at 5% p.a.; negligence penalty up to 25% of tax understated; intentional evasion penalty up to three times tax evaded (Art. 96 VAT Act); criminal fine up to CHF 30,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal and cantonal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung) with signed annual accounts, tax reconciliation schedules, and warehouse-related reserves documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered office canton (e.g., Zug, Zurich, Geneva); Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for direct federal tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Cantonal deadline generally set at 6 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year taxpayer: 31 March to 30 June depending on canton); extension to September/October routinely granted on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 3.5% p.a. on federal tax and 3-5% p.a. cantonal; procedural late-filing fine up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 174 DBG); negligence fine up to 25% and intentional evasion fine up to three times tax evaded; estimated assessment at taxpayer's disadvantage; enforced collection and potential court-ordered liquidation on persistent default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and OASI/DI/EO (AHV/IV/EO) contribution settlement for warehouse, cross-dock, and administrative staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) of the registered office canton; Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) for statistical and conformity purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Individual Lohnausweis for employees by 31 January; annual employer wage settlement and contribution reconciliation with the Compensation Office per its circular, generally by 31 January through 28 February; contributions prepaid quarterly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 5% p.a. on arrears; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 86 AHVG; statutory personal liability of directors and officers for unpaid employer contributions under Art. 87 AHVG

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership declaration and Commercial Register notifications for any change in directors, share capital, registered shares, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) and the Swiss Transparency Register for beneficial ownership information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO changes: within 30 days of becoming known; pre-existing AGs completed initial Transparency Register registration by 31 December 2024; no Swiss equivalent of the annual confirmation statement exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to CHF 10,000 for failure to notify the Commercial Register (Art. 943 CO); UBO non-disclosure penalty up to CHF 10,000 under the AML Act; change filings additionally attract late-filing surcharges and reinstatement costs if deregistered

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit (ordentliche Revision) is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of three thresholds in two consecutive years: CHF 40 million balance sheet total, CHF 80 million net turnover, 250 full-time employees (thresholds effective 1 January 2024; previously CHF 20m / CHF 40m / 250 FTE). Below these thresholds the AG must appoint a limited auditor (eingeschränkte Revision) unless shareholders unanimously resolve an audit opt-out each fiscal year. A cross-dock / overseas-warehouse 3PL entity without significant owned property or captive fleet will typically remain below the full-audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957-963b) for non-listed companies; Swiss GAAP FER for medium and large entities; IFRS mandatory for listed top-tier entities. Accounts must be drawn in CHF and provide a true and fair view, with notes, income statement, balance sheet, and cash-flow statement as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law uses a change-based rather than annual-confirmation model. The Transparency Register, operative since April 2024 under the AML Act (Art. 62a-62j), requires initial UBO declaration; subsequent changes in beneficial ownership, including share transfers affecting control, must be reported within 30 days of the company becoming aware. The Board must review and update the internal UBO file at each AGM and retain supporting transfer documentation. There is no public access to the Transparency Register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Aktienbuch (Share Register of registered shares and holders)
Minute book for General Meetings and Board resolutions
UBO documentation file including share-transfer evidence and Transparency Register filings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,500 (annual fiduciary charge in Zug, Zurich, or Geneva for registered office, registered agent, mail forwarding, and basic secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 12,000 for a limited audit; USD 12,000 - 30,000 for a full statutory audit, depending on warehouse transaction volume, headcount, and intercompany flow complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal statutory rate plus cantonal/communal profit taxes; aggregate effective rate 11.9%–21% depending on canton (approx. 11.9% in Zug, 14.0% in Zurich, 21.0% in Geneva)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Cantonal/communal tax holidays up to 10 years for genuinely new businesses; federal and cantonal patent box regimes reducing qualifying IP income by 90%; R&D super-deduction of up to 150% of eligible costs; participation relief for qualified dividends and capital gains at both federal and cantonal levels; notional interest deduction in some cantons

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Unified federal and cantonal corporate tax return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale personnes morales), filed electronically via the SwissTax portal or cantonal eTax portals (e.g., Zug OW4/GETAX); federal tax return incorporated in the same filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; extensions of up to 3 additional months granted on written request; provisional payments are due quarterly during the tax year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: commercial register entry, UID/EUR business identifier, legal form, seat, and address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must provide full legal name, country of residence, and shareholding percentage; attach incorporation certificates and power of attorney if represented

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates, calendar years or merchant quarterly accounting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the reporting period matches the audited financial statements and cross-border consolidation reports; ensure consistency with home-country fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial net profit to taxable net income: add back non-deductible expenses (entertainment, taxes, reserves) and deduct tax-privileged income (participation, patent box)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled companies should attach transfer pricing schedules and arm's-length documentation for intragroup invoicing, warehouse fees, and logistics margins

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation relief deduction: gross dividends and capital gains on qualifying participations (≥10% of nominal share capital, held at least 1 year) deducted at federal and cantonal level
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List underlying foreign entities and attach source-country dividend statements; treaty withholding rates and source taxes on those dividends must be declared separately

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits: Swiss federal anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) withheld on Swiss-source income and recoverable tax credits on foreign source income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities claiming treaty benefits must submit Forms 85/82 and a valid tax residence certificate (TRC); without TRC, no credit or refund is permitted

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CHF 50–1,000 per tax period; repeated or wilful non-filing subject to additional fines up to CHF 10,000; deferred payment interest accrues at 3.5% p.a. (default surcharge); criminal penalties for intentional non-filing or evasion of up to 3 times the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends distributed by an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) to shareholders, regardless of the shareholder's residence
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty reduction or refund, the foreign shareholder must (i) hold shares for a minimum 12-month period where the treaty requires, (ii) submit a completed Form 82 (refund application) or Form 85 (advance relief) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), (iii) attach an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's competent authority, (iv) provide bank confirmation of custodies, and (v) file within 3 years of the dividend payment for refunds; Swiss domestic participation relief already exempts qualified dividends from corporate income tax, but the 35% WHT is generally refunded only under a DTA unless the distribution is made to a qualifying Swiss shareholder
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT of 35% applies only to interest on bonds and money market instruments issued by Swiss borrowers; ordinary trade interest, bank loans, and intercompany loans are not subject to Swiss withholding tax; royalties for IP licenses are not subject to Swiss source withholding tax; under most comprehensive Swiss DTAs (e.g., France, Germany, USA, UK, China) royalty rates are 0%–10% and interest rates 0%–10%, but a 0% source WHT on interest is typical; treaties do not override the Swiss 35% anticipatory tax on bond interest without prior approval

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss tax law does not codify a formal local-file/master-file threshold; however, the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and cantonal authorities require documentation on request where intragroup transactions exceed CHF 1 million in aggregate, or where the transaction volume is material; CbC reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of CHF 900 million or more in the prior fiscal year (consistent with OECD minimum standards). A simplified Single-Entity documentation file is sufficient for related-party transactions below CHF 1 million aggregate and CHF 200,000 for interest/royalties
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Swiss courts and administrative practice apply a substance-over-form doctrine; an enterprise must demonstrate real economic activity (office premises, operational employees, actual logistics functions, and risk management) to retain tax residence and treaty benefits. Entities acting as 'letterbox' or sham companies with no substance are recharacterized, denied treaty access, and treated as transparent for Swiss tax purposes, triggering reassessment, penalties, and revocation of the AG's business license

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income from overseas warehouse operations, undervaluation of stock, misclassification of capital gains as tax-exempt participation income, or false booking of related-party debts leading to understated Swiss taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of income tax plus interest at 3.5%; administrative penalty up to 3 times the evaded tax (Art. 175 Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act); criminal fine for attempted evasion; repeat offenders risk publicity of penalty decisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or management officers who knowingly sign false tax returns are jointly and severally liable for the imposed penalties; criminal convictions may lead to imprisonment of up to 3 years (or 10 years for qualified aggravated tax fraud under Art. 186 DBG), travel ban, and confiscation of personal assets

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Swiss AG exists only as a nominal booking vehicle for a foreign parent, lacks qualified personnel and decision-making, holds no financial risk, and has no physical office or logistics management in Switzerland; treaty-shopping structure where the sole purpose is to receive dividends / royalties and re-route them offshore
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the AG as a transparent pass-through entity, denial of Swiss treaty benefits, full reassessment of profits in the hands of the direct shareholder, and revocation of the business license; administrative fine up to CHF 20,000 under anti-abuse and register provisions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil allows creditors and tax authorities to hold directors personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes; directors also face Swiss criminal prosecution for organized tax evasion (Art. 327 of the Swiss Penal Code) with imprisonment up to 5 years and deprivation of travel documents

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting cross-border warehouse service fees, storage margins, and intercompany logistics charges outside the arm's length range; failure to submit transfer pricing documentation upon request; unjustifiable profit shifting to zero/low-tax jurisdictions through management fees or inflated cost-plus charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increasing Swiss taxable income; recategorization of the excess as a constructive dividend subject to 35% withholding tax and federal/ cantonal penalty interest; documentation penalty of 10% of the adjustment, up to CHF 100,000; for serious cases additional assessment up to 3 times the additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing directors who approve or execute non-arm's-length intragroup contracts are personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax on constructive dividends and related penalties; criminal proceedings for falsification of accounts may result in imprisonment up to 3 years and permanent exclusion from serving as director in Switzerland

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Fraud / Failure to Collect
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of dividends or bond interest, or payment of constructively taxable capital distributions, without withholding and remitting the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax to the ESTV; false declarations that shareholders qualify for treaty exemption absent valid TRC or holding period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Full collection of the unpaid withholding tax plus interest of 3.5% p.a.; administrative penalty up to 3 times the amount evaded; elimination of shareholder rights (voting and dividend claims) for tax-evading beneficiaries; limited statute of limitations of 10 years but extended to 15 years for intentional fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and personally liable for the full withholding tax debt if they fail to collect and remit, irrespective of corporate insolvency; criminal prosecution for unlawful issuance of dividends leads to imprisonment up to 3 years; travel bans and asset freezes are routinely imposed during criminal investigations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the 3PL cross-dock warehousing operation to move goods or cash derived from foreign tax evasion, foreign exchange control fraud, or organised crime; failing to perform AML due diligence on non-resident customers and accepting opaque payments through unattributed high-risk shell entities or virtual assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), failure to identify beneficial owners and report suspicious transactions results in fines up to CHF 200,000; confiscation of all proceeds; criminal offense for serious cases leads to imprisonment up to 3 years; the firm's license to operate a financial intermediary, if any, is revoked
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who deliberately turn a blind eye to laundered funds or sign false declaration forms commit or are accomplices to money laundering (Art. 305bis Swiss Penal Code) and face imprisonment of up to 3 years (extended to 10 years for qualified money laundering); civil liability requires personal restitution of unpaid taxes plus damages; travel bans and bank account freezes apply
